title: Variables and loops (demo lesson)
intro: Work through each activity in order. Press Save my work regularly — the chip at the top shows whether your latest changes are saved.

blocks.html:
Starter

A variable is a named space in memory that stores a value. A loop repeats instructions. Answer the questions below, then try the code.

blocks.prompt: 1. In your own words, what is a variable?
blocks.criteria: A good answer says a variable is a named location/space in memory that stores a value, and ideally that the value can change while the program runs.

blocks.prompt: 2. Why is a for loop better than copying and pasting the same line five times?
blocks.criteria: A good answer mentions less repeated code, easier to change (edit once), fewer mistakes, and that the number of repeats can be controlled by a value/variable.

blocks.task: Run this program, then change it so it adds up the numbers 1 to 100 instead of the prices.
blocks.starter:
prices = [3, 5, 2, 8]
total = 0
for p in prices:
    total = total + p
print("Total:", total)
